To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the reputation of a horticultural product line is influenced primarily by sensory attributes, and (ii) price variation or bandwidth of a product line is controlled by the sensory attributes of appearance and colour, and the objective attribute of package weight.

price variation in the horticultural industry is a complex phenomenon that is influenced by a variety of factors and that price is a function of the reputation of a particular product line and its price bandwidth.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the development of a theoretical framework for price-quality relationships; (ii) the identification of factors which influence price and quality; and (iii) the development of an empirical model for price prediction.
the analysis of the effect on the price of horticultural products of: the supply of produce; the reputation of the product; and the price bandwidth.
the analysis of price data, the effect of reputation on prices, the effect of supply on prices, and the effect of quality (particularly sensory) on prices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reputation of the product line, the sensory quality of the product, the supply and demand and the price bandwidth are all significant in determining price levels and variation.
the reputation of any particular line, and hence the average price of that line, is controlled primarily by the composite sensory attributes of that product line.
quality is the most important factor affecting the price of a particular horticultural produce.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reputation of horticultural product lines is determined primarily by the composite sensory qualities, and that the price bandwidth is determined by the objective quality attributes.
quality is the most important factor in determining prices for horticultural produce, and that it is a complex attribute.

the price-quality relationship in horticultural products is complex, but that the price of a particular product line is a function of its reputation and its bandwidth, both of which are influenced by sensory quality attributes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reputation of the product line is an important influence on the average price.
price and price variation are determined by the interaction of many factors, including the attributes of quality, the reputation of a line, and the supply-demand situation at any particular time.
the price of horticultural products is a reflection of the quality of the product and the reputation of the product in the market place.
